title: Algebraic upper shriek: polynomial models, coinduction, composition and flat base change
statement: For a finite type map $\varphi:R\to A$ of commutative Noetherian rings, choose a polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$. There is a functor $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$, well defined up to isomorphism, whose chosen presentation model is $R\operatorname{Hom}_{P}(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$ for $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Here $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,-)$ denotes derived coinduction with its natural $A$-module structure. The following comparisons hold. (i) For a surjection $\varphi$, $\varphi^!=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,-)$, right adjoint to restriction of scalars; forgetting the $A$-action gives the ordinary derived Hom over $R$. For any ring maps $R\to B\to C$, derived coinduction composes canonically, compatibly with its evaluation counits. (ii) For finite type Noetherian maps $R\xrightarrow{a}B\xrightarrow{b}C$, there is an isomorphism $b^!a^!K\cong(ba)^!K$ for $K\in D^+(R)$; the identity map can be modeled by the identity functor. (iii) For a flat map $R\to R'$ of Noetherian rings, $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ and $\varphi':R'\to A'$, there is an isomorphism $\varphi^!K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\cong(\varphi')^!(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R')$ for $K\in D^+(R)$. (iv) If $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an open immersion, then $\varphi^!K\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$. These assertions concern chosen polynomial models and isomorphisms, and do not assert a canonical orientation for different polynomial presentations.

source.place: Tags 0BZI, 0BZJ (polynomial construction and well-definedness), 0A70, 0A71, 0C0F (derived coinduction), 0BZN (flat base change), 0BZT (composition), 0C0H (open localization).

proof.text: Use ordinary module complexes throughout, identifying modules with sheaves on a one-object ringed site. For any map $T\to B$, choose a K-injective $T$-resolution $K\to I$; these exist because module categories are Grothendieck. Give $\operatorname{Hom}_T(B,I)$ the action $(b h)(b')=h(b'b)$, and call its derived object $C_B^T(K)$. The degreewise adjunction is explicitly $v\mapsto(m\mapsto[b\mapsto v(bm)])$, with inverse evaluation at $1$. It is an adjunction of Hom complexes, so if $N$ is an acyclic $B$-complex then $\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(N,\operatorname{Hom}_T(B,I))=\operatorname{Hom}_T^\bullet(N,I)$ is acyclic. Thus the coinduced complex is K-injective over $B$. The K-injective Hom-bijection on both sides descends this adjunction to $D(B)\to D(T)$ and $C_B^T$. Changing K-injective resolutions gives homotopy-equivalent outputs: a quasi-isomorphism of K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence by that same bijection. This makes $C_B^T$ a functor, right adjoint to restriction, with counit $h\mapsto h(1)$. On forgetting the action its model is exactly $R\operatorname{Hom}_T(B,K)$ by the definition of derived Hom.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext); the K-injective model and explicit ordinary adjunction.

proof.text: For $T\to B\to C$, the composite coinduction on a K-injective $I$ is computed by $\operatorname{Hom}_B(C,\operatorname{Hom}_T(B,I))$, since step 1 makes the inner complex K-injective. The chain isomorphism from $\operatorname{Hom}_T(C,I)$ sends $h$ to $(c\mapsto[b\mapsto h(bc)])$; its inverse is $v\mapsto(c\mapsto v(c)(1))$. Both maps are $C$-linear and commute with differentials. The composite of the two counits is $v\mapsto v(1)(1)$, exactly evaluation of the inverse image at $1\in C$. This proves the canonical composition comparison, with its counit compatibility, for arbitrary ring maps and unbounded complexes.

Let $T\to B=T/(s)$ have $s$ a nonzerodivisor. If $B=0$, both coinduction and tensor with $B$ are zero, proving the claim immediately; assume $B\ne0$ for the regular-sequence calculation. The two-term resolution $[T\xrightarrow{s}T]$ in degrees $-1,0$ makes $B$ perfect over $T$. The sequence $(s)$ is Koszul-regular, and its conormal has basis $\bar s$ by the cited regular-sequence results. The dual Koszul calculation gives $H^i(C_B^T(T))=0$ for $i\ne1$ and $H^1(C_B^T(T))\cong B$, with its $B$-action, by evaluating the dual of $\bar s$. Since an object with only one cohomology module is isomorphic to that module in its cohomological degree, $C_B^T(T)\cong B[-1]$ in $D(B)$. The perfect-algebra coinduction tensor comparison therefore gives $C_B^T(L)\cong L\otimes_T^{\mathbf L}B[-1]$ for every $L\in D(T)$.

For a chosen $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, define $F_P(K)=C_A^P(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$; extension of scalars is a functor on all of $D(R)$. Compare it with $Q=P[y]\twoheadrightarrow A$. Lift the image of $y$ to $g\in P$, and let $\pi:Q\twoheadrightarrow P$ send $y$ to $g$. Multiplication by $y-g$ is injective: the leading nonzero coefficient of a polynomial survives multiplication by this monic polynomial. Compute scalar extensions using a K-flat $R$-representative $F$; $F\otimes_RQ$ is K-flat over $Q$ since its tensor with an acyclic $Q$-complex is $F$ tensored with that underlying $R$-complex. The termwise identity $(F\otimes_RQ)\otimes_QP=F\otimes_RP$ and step 3 give $C_P^Q(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)[1]\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P$. Apply $C_A^P$ and step 2 to get $F_Q\cong F_P$, including the shift $[n]$. Iterating treats any finite number of added variables. Any two presentations $P_1,P_2$ have the common polynomial presentation $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_m]\twoheadrightarrow A$; surjectivity supplies all the necessary lifts. Comparing each with the common presentation proves well-definedness up to isomorphism of functors. We claim no independence of the chosen lifts, orientation, or canonical comparisons between different presentations.

When $R\twoheadrightarrow A$ is surjective, take the zero-variable presentation $P=R$. Its model is $C_A^R$, so step 1 proves all assertions in (i) concerning that map. For $A=R$ this complex is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,I)\cong I$ by evaluation, so the identity map has identity model. The arbitrary-ring composition assertion of (i) was proved in step 2.

source.place: Tag 0BZI, surjective and identity cases; Tags 0A70, 0A71, 0C0F.

proof.text: We record the hypotheses needed for flat base change. A finite polynomial algebra $P$ over the Noetherian ring $R$ is Noetherian by the finite-type-algebra Noetherian theorem: use the presentation with zero kernel. The same applies to every finite polynomial algebra used below, over $R$, $B$, or a Noetherian $R'$. A quotient $A$ of $P$ is generated by $1$ as a $P$-module. The finite-free-resolution theorem gives a bounded-above finite-free resolution of this module, so $A[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $P$. Polynomial extension is flat: its monomial basis makes tensor with it a direct sum of copies of the original module, preserving injections. For any flat map $P\to P'$ and $A'=A\otimes_PP'$, the equality $N\otimes_AA'=N\otimes_PP'$ for $A$-modules shows $A\to A'$ flat as well.

source.place: Tag 0BZN hypotheses; algebra.tex Tags 00FN (finite type over Noetherian) and 00LP (finite-free resolutions).

proof.text: For the quotient $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ and a flat map $P\to P'$, define a comparison $C_A^P(M)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to C_{A'}^{P'}(M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P')$ by the coinduction adjunction of step 1. Its adjunct is the scalar extension of the evaluation counit $C_A^P(M)\to M$. Indeed, after restriction to $P'$, the source is the ordinary tensor $C_A^P(M)\otimes_PP'$: both extension functors are exact by flatness, and the identification is $h\otimes(a\otimes p')\mapsto ah\otimes p'$. Forgetting the $A'$-action, the resulting comparison is precisely $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,M)\otimes_PP'\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{P'}(A\otimes_PP',M\otimes_PP')$, since the adjunction counit is evaluation at $1$. If $M\in D^+(P)$, step 6 verifies the pseudo-coherence hypothesis and the flat derived-Hom base-change lemma makes this map an isomorphism. Restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms, because the underlying cohomology modules of a cone are unchanged. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism in $D(A')$, not just after forgetting its action.

source.place: Section 0E28 (section-base-change-trivial-duality), Equation 0E29 and Tags 0E2A (lemma-check-base-change-is-iso), 0BZM (lemma-flat-bc-surjection); evaluation description of the map.

proof.text: For (iii), base-change the chosen presentation to $P'=R'[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. The map $P\to P'$ is flat since tensor with $P'$ over $P$ is tensor with $R'$ over $R$ on restricted modules. If $K\in D^+(R)$, then $M=(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]\in D^+(P)$, since $P$ is $R$-free. Apply step 7. The two coefficient complexes agree because $(K\otimes_R P)\otimes_PP'=K\otimes_RP'=(K\otimes_RR')\otimes_{R'}P'$, computed by exact flat extensions. This gives exactly the displayed isomorphism of (iii). Step 4 permits replacing either chosen presentation model by any other one.

source.place: Tag 0BZN (lemma-flat-bc), including the double-base-change identity of more-algebra.tex Tag 08YU.

proof.text:
For (ii), choose $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$, choose generators $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ of $C$ over $B$, and put $Q=P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, $Q'=B[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$. Let $\chi:Q'\twoheadrightarrow C$ send $y_j$ to $c_j$. For $M=K\otimes_RP$ with $K\in D^+(R)$, step 7 applied to the flat map $P\to Q$ gives $C_B^P(M)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}Q'\cong C_{Q'}^Q(M\otimes_PQ)$. Apply $C_C^{Q'}$; step 2 identifies its composite with $C_C^Q$. Adding the shifts gives
$$b^!a^!K\cong C_C^{Q'}(C_{Q'}^Q(K\otimes_RQ))[n+m]\cong C_C^Q(K\otimes_RQ)[n+m]=(ba)^!K.$$
Here $Q$ has exactly $n+m$ variables over $R$ and surjects onto $C$. Thus the chosen polynomial models give the asserted comparison; step 4 gives it for any other model. Zero generators are allowed in either factor.

source.place: Tag 0BZT (lemma-composition-shriek-algebraic); the scalar extension in its first displayed line must be by Q′=B[y], not by Q=P[y].

proof.text: If $A=0$, the open-immersion assertion is immediate: $D(A)$ is the zero category and both functors are zero. Henceforth assume $A\ne0$. Suppose now $j:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an open immersion. By its definition all stalk homomorphisms are isomorphisms, so they are flat; the affine flatness criterion makes $R\to A$ flat. Its stalks therefore have Tor dimension zero: apply the flat-resolution Tor comparison to the length-zero flat resolution. The one-member affine cover makes $\operatorname{Spec}R$ locally Noetherian by definition; the spectrum quasi-compactness lemma makes it Noetherian. Since $j$ is finite type by the standing hypothesis, the affine polynomial-resolution theorem supplies a finite projective $P$-resolution of $A$ for the chosen $P\twoheadrightarrow A$. Step 6 also supplies a finite-free resolution. Truncate this latter resolution at its projective syzygy using the cited kernel-projectivity theorem; the syzygy is finitely generated because $P$ is Noetherian. This is a bounded finite-projective resolution, so $A$ is perfect over $P$. If the projective dimension is zero, use $A[0]$ itself. All these facts hold without $R$ being regular.

source.place: Tag 0C0H (lemma-upper-shriek-localize), perfect polynomial model for its unbounded form; more-morphisms.tex Tag 069C; algebra.tex Tags 00LP, 00O5. Properties Tag 01OV; Algebra Tag 00E8.

proof.text: The open immersion is a monomorphism: two maps to its open subscheme with the same composite have the same underlying map and sheaf map, since the inclusion restricts the structure sheaf. Hence its self fibre product is itself. The affine-fibre-product theorem identifies the resulting multiplication map $A\otimes_RA\to A$ as an isomorphism, with both coprojections identified with the identity. Set $P_A=P\otimes_RA=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and write $a_i$ for the images of $x_i$ in $A$. The scalar extension of $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ is the evaluation $P_A\to A$, $x_i\mapsto a_i$, since $A\otimes_RA=A$. Its kernel is generated by $x_i-a_i$: subtracting the evaluation of a polynomial gives a sum of multiples of these differences. Successively quotienting by the first $i$ differences leaves a polynomial ring over $A$ in the remaining variables, and the next difference is monic. Thus this sequence is Koszul-regular; its conormal basis is the classes of these differences. The dual Koszul theorem gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_{P_A}(A,P_A)\cong A[-n]$, as an underlying $P_A$-complex; its sole nonzero cohomology is identified $A$-linearly using the ordered conormal generator.

source.place: Tag 0C0H, self-base-change argument; explicit polynomial graph resolution, using duality.tex Tag 0BQZ.

proof.text: Put $\omega=C_A^P(P)[n]\in D(A)$. Apply the existing perfect derived-Hom base-change theorem to $P\to P_A$, the perfect $P$-complex $A[0]$ from step 10, and target $P[0]$. Flatness identifies the base-changed first argument with $A\otimes_RA=A$. The scalar extension of the underlying $P$-complex of $\omega$ therefore has cohomology $A$ in degree $0$ and zero elsewhere, by step 11. On the other hand extension by $P_A$ on that complex is extension by $A$ over $R$. For every $A$-module $N$, multiplication $N\otimes_RA\to N$ is an isomorphism because $A\otimes_RA=A$; flatness of $A/R$ makes this true for complexes without a bound. Thus $\omega$ itself has cohomology only in degree $0$, and $H^0(\omega)\cong A$. This is $A$-linear: the coefficient action of $A\subset P_A$ agrees with the original action under the equality of the two coprojections into $A\otimes_RA$, and the top Koszul identification is linear for that action. Consequently truncation gives $\omega\cong A[0]$ in $D(A)$. We do not attempt to lift an arbitrary isomorphism after forgetting the action.

source.place: Tag 0C0H, base change by the open immersion itself; more-algebra.tex Tag 0A6A, perfect case.

proof.text:
For arbitrary $K\in D(R)$, apply the perfect-algebra coinduction tensor comparison to $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P$. It gives
$$\varphi^!K\cong (K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}\omega\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\omega\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A.$$
The middle equality preserves the $A$-action: choose a K-flat $R$-representative $F$ of $K$; $F\otimes_RP$ is K-flat over $P$ by the identity $(F\otimes_RP)\otimes_PN=F\otimes_RN$, and rebracket $(F\otimes_RP)\otimes_P\omega=F\otimes_R\omega$ termwise. The last equality is induced by step 12 using the derived tensor functor with an $A$-complex. This proves (iv) on the full unbounded category. The empty open has $A=0$ and gives the zero functor; $n=0$ is the empty Koszul complex and requires no shift. Together with steps 4--9 this proves all clauses with their stated bounds.

source.place: Tag 0C0H, with Tag 0BZE for the unbounded tensor calculation and Tag 0A6A perfect base change.
